Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub walk in with their blades for Pakistan. Nandre Burger has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

It was left to the skipper, Shaheen Shah Afridi, to apply the final, clinical blow. He came back and, with two wickets in two balls, getting rid of Peter and Lungi Ngidi. He wrapped up the innings in a flash! South Africa are all out for a mere 143. Pakistan's bowlers, with Abrar the star and great support from Afridi, Nawaz, and Agha, have completed a demolition job. The home side now needs a very comfortable 144 runs to clinch the series! Stay tuned for the chase...

The real damage, however, was inflicted by the brilliant Abrar Ahmed. The spinner was absolutely unplayable, weaving a web around the middle order and sparking a devastating collapse. He tore through the line-up, grabbing four wickets in quick succession to register his career-best figures of 4/27. The Proteas simply had no answer to the turning ball, losing wickets in a rush and slumping to 130/8. Only a brief resistance from Nqaba Peter kept the score ticking over.

South Africa have been bowled out for a mere 143 runs! South Africa, having opted to bat, got off to a flying start thanks to the veteran Quinton de Kock and Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who smashed 72 runs for the opening wicket. They looked comfortable until the Pakistani spin attack was introduced. Salman Ali Agha provided the crucial double breakthrough, removing Pretorius and de Zorzi, which immediately opened the floodgates. QDK brought up his fifty but couldn't stick around, and the South African innings began to lose its momentum dramatically.

OUT! TIMBER! Two in two for the skipper. A job extremely well done for the hosts. A yorker, on middle, Lungi Ngidi looks to block it but gets beaten as the ball hits the stumps. South Africa have been bowled out for a mere 143 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: All set for action. The Pakistani players are out in the middle. Quinton de Kock and Lhuan-dre Pretorius to open for South Africa. The Eagle, Shaheen Afridi to bowl first. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Urooj Mumtaz feels the surface is very dry and there could be a lot of natural variations for both the pacers and the spinners. Vernon Philander joins and states that the big scoring options are going to be in the first 15 overs. Reckons scoring zones are going to be more straighter than squarer.

Shaheen Afridi, the captain of Pakistan says they were looking to bowl first. Adds few decisions didn't go their way in the last game. Shares winning always feels good so we will try to give our best here. Informs that Naseem Shah and Mohammad Wasim are rested, Abrar Ahmed and Haris Rauf are in.

South Africa's captain, Matthew Breetzke says they will bat first, feels the wicket is very used, so they will like to put a score on the board and try and defend it. Shares in a game like this, runs on the board are important. Reckons over 290 would be a good score but they'll assess the conditions in the first 10 overs. Informs that they have one last-minute change, Sinethemba Qeshile misses out due to injury, Rubin Hermann makes his debut, while Lungi Ngidi comes in for George Linde.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Salman Agha, Hussain Talat, Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi (C), Abrar Ahmed (In for Mohammad Wasim), Haris Rauf (In for Naseem Shah).

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Tony de Zorzi, Rubin Hermann (In for Sinethemba Qeshile), Matthew Breetzke (C), Donovan Ferreira, Corbin Bosch, Bjorn Fortuin, Nandre Burger, Nqabayomzi Peter, Lungi Ngidi (In for George Linde).
TOSS - South Africa have won the toss and will BAT first!

Today, everything is on the line! Will Pakistan finally get the decisive win in front of their home crowd, fueled by Haris Rauf's return? Or will Quinton de Kock and the Proteas cap off their demanding tour with a stunning series victory? Tune in for what is sure to be an epic series decider! The stage is set, the teams are ready. Stay tuned for further updates.

The second ODI saw Pakistan post a competitive 269/9, built on solid fifties from Salman Agha, Saim Ayub, and a blazing half-century from Mohammad Nawaz, despite a devastating new-ball spell from the Proteas' Nandre Burger. But the South African chase was all about dominance. De Kock hammered a magnificent, unbeaten 123, brilliantly supported by Tony de Zorzi's quickfire 76, as they powered to a comprehensive eight-wicket victory.

Pakistan will be buzzing with excitement as their gun pacer, Haris Rauf, is back and available for selection after his two-match ban. His return adds significant firepower to the bowling attack as the Men in Green look to close out the series victory. However, South Africa has proven their resilience throughout this tour, even though they haven't won a single toss! They bounced back brilliantly in the second ODI, chasing down a challenging target with ease, thanks to a masterclass century from the returning Quinton de Kock.

Get ready for a massive Saturday of cricket! The tension is sky-high as both the T20I series between Australia and India, and the crucial ODI series between Pakistan and South Africa, reach their grand finales today. All eyes are fixed on the Iqbal Stadium in Faisalabad where Pakistan and South Africa clash in the third and final ODI. ...MATCH DAY...

The three-match One Day International series between Pakistan and South Africa has lived up to its billing, leading to a thrilling winner-takes-all 3rd ODI at the Iqbal Stadium in Faisalabad. With the series perfectly poised at 1-1, this final encounter not only determines the series winner but also serves as a crucial measuring stick for both teams as they begin to shape their ODI plans for the road to the next ICC Cricket World Cup. The return of international cricket to the historic Iqbal Stadium after 17 years has been met with two captivating contests and it wouldn't be wrong to predict another close contest in the final game. The two matches played suggest a surface that is initially tricky for batting, offering some assistance to the pacers early on. However, once settled, batters can make big scores, particularly in the later overs. The dew factor at this venue, especially this time of the year, is significant and has historically favored the chasing side, making the toss a crucial factor for the captains. Pakistan's captain, Shaheen Afridi, has seen two very different performances from his team. While the fight shown in the first ODI was commendable, the collapse in the second match, where they were reduced to 22/3, is a major concern. The onus is heavily on the star trio of Fakhar Zaman, Babar Azam, and Mohammad Rizwan to fire. The middle order, led by the in-form Salman Agha, has shown resilience, but they cannot constantly be relied upon for rescue acts. South Africa's dominant performance in the 2nd ODI, spearheaded by their returning veteran Quinton de Kock, has shifted the momentum firmly in their favor. His magnificent, effortless century in the last game proved why he is still an indispensable asset. The pace duo of Nandre Burger and Lungi Ngidi, who have each played a match each, has been superb, with Burger's four-wicket haul dismantling Pakistan's top order in the previous game. The young wrist-spinner Nqabayomzi Peter also impressed, adding a valuable wicket-taking dimension in the middle. The first 10 overs in both innings will be crucial as they will test whether Pakistan's top order can provide a platform for the middle order and also if Shaheen Afridi and co can break through the Proteas' explosive top order and set things rolling with the ball. Who do you think will clinch the series win?
